name: lpqi_spad64_pathfinder
label: LPQI-Pathfinder IMSE 64x64 test SPAD array in the NOT / TNG cameras (500 ps, 6.7e6 cps capture ceiling)
sources: R. Content (LPQI optical scientist), email to P. Nugent 2026-11-05: the 64x64 SPAD's efficiency is 71 % at 422 nm and 16 % at 550 nm
F. Prada (LPQI PI), email to P. Nugent 2026-10-07: the array with its optics collects the star on a few pixels; 6.7e6 cps capture ceiling; 500 ps White Rabbit timing target

Content et al. 2026, Proc. SPIE 14148, 1414832: the Pathfinder cameras image the star on a cluster of four sensitive areas with the filter in a collimated beam; a 25 %-fill-factor detector with < 0.5 ns timing is in production
Quintana et al. 2026, Sensors 26, 5757: the published array (lpqi_spad64_i2cass) this one extends
notes: The 64x64 TEST array of the LPQI-Pathfinder cameras, as used for the 2026-11 filter decision (550.0 nm, 0.5 nm; backends lpqi_pf64_550_0p5 and lpqi_mpd_550_0p5). The MPD single pixel (lpqi_spad1_mpd) is the science detector; this array is for tests and is not the sensor of the final instruments (detectors/lpqi_spad64_i2cass_nextgen).

PDE: the two values R. Content quoted, 0.71 at 422 nm and 0.16 at 550 nm, taken as the end-to-end efficiency (optical coupling onto the sensitive areas = 1). They replace the flat 0.50 over 400-550 nm (F. Prada 2026-10-07) used until 2026-11-05, which made the array 3x too efficient at 550 nm.

If the two values are the sensor's photon-detection probability alone, multiply the table by the coupling: 0.67 reproduces the 0.50 peak quoted for microlenses, and the SPIE paper gives about 0.21 for a star imaged on a cluster of four sensitive areas of the 3.5 %-fill chip. Nights scale as 1/coupling^2 where the array is photon-limited.

Between 422 and 550 nm the table is linear; 400 nm is set to the 422 nm value; beyond 550 nm it continues the 422-to-550 nm fall as an exponential (e-folding 86 nm). All three are ASSUMED pending the measured curve.

500 ps FWHM is the White Rabbit time-stamping target (the SPIE paper quotes 1 ns for the present chip and < 0.5 ns for the one in production); 6.7e6 cps is the implemented capture ceiling for the whole array; n_pixels 4 is the cluster the star is imaged on.
assumptions: pde_table_nm (two quoted points; coupling 1; interpolation and red tail)
